behavioral_notes.observation: OAuth2 authorization-code flow against the Microsoft identity platform, with the whole token lifecycle hosted on an AbstractModel mixin (microsoft.outlook.mixin) rather than on a business object. _compute_outlook_uri builds the consent URL via _get_microsoft_endpoint() (ir.config_parameter microsoft_outlook.endpoint, default https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/) + 'authorize?...' with response_type=code, redirect_uri=/microsoft_outlook/confirm and scope 'openid email offline_access https://outlook.office.com/User.read {_OUTLOOK_SCOPE}' (offline_access is what makes Microsoft return a refresh_token); state carries model/id + an hmac CSRF token. _fetch_outlook_refresh_token POSTs grant_type=authorization_code to the same endpoint's 'token' path and returns (refresh_token, access_token, expiration=now+expires_in); _fetch_outlook_access_token POSTs grant_type=refresh_token to get a rotated (refresh_token, access_token, id_token, expiration). Tokens are persisted as microsoft_outlook_refresh_token / _access_token / _access_token_expiration on the mail-server record itself (all groups='base.group_system', copy=False). On a non-OK HTTP response the JSON error_description is surfaced as a UserError. None of this token machinery is visible from field/model metadata.

The single authentication primitive shared by SMTP and IMAP. _generate_outlook_oauth2_string(login) checks microsoft_outlook_access_token_expiration against now + OUTLOOK_TOKEN_VALIDITY_THRESHOLD (OUTLOOK_TOKEN_REQUEST_TIMEOUT 5s + 5 = 10s); if the access token is missing/expired it calls _fetch_outlook_access_token(refresh_token) to mint a fresh one (writing back the rotated refresh_token + access_token + expiration on the record), otherwise it reuses the cached token. With no refresh_token at all it raises 'Please connect with your Outlook account before using it.' It returns the SASL XOAUTH2 argument exactly as 'user=%s\x01auth=Bearer %s\x01\x01'. This just-in-time refresh-on-send and the SASL framing are runtime behavior absent from metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: ir.mail_server._smtp_login__ (XOAUTH2 over SMTP) and fetchmail.server._imap_login__ (XOAUTH2 over IMAP)
behavioral_notes.observation: Both transports replace password auth with bearer-token auth by overriding the base login hooks. ir.mail_server (_OUTLOOK_SCOPE = https://outlook.office.com/SMTP.Send) overrides _smtp_login__: when smtp_authentication=='outlook' it base64-encodes _generate_outlook_oauth2_string(smtp_user) and issues connection.ehlo() then connection.docmd('AUTH', f'XOAUTH2 {oauth_param}') instead of the inherited login; @api.constrains forbids a non-empty smtp_pass, forces smtp_encryption='starttls' and requires smtp_user, and onchange pins smtp_host=smtp.outlook.com / port 587 / from_filter=smtp_user. Outlook also gets a lower personal send-rate cap (mail.server.personal.limit.minutes_outlook, default 10) because Outlook flags bursts as spam. fetchmail.server (_OUTLOOK_SCOPE = https://outlook.office.com/IMAP.AccessAsUser.All) overrides _imap_login__: for server_type=='outlook' it calls connection.authenticate('XOAUTH2', lambda x: auth_string) then selects INBOX, pins server=imap.outlook.com / SSL / port 993 and forces _get_connection_type()->'imap'. The substitution of XOAUTH2 for the inherited password path at the protocol layer is pure code behavior.

behavioral_notes.element: OAuth redirect/authorize config flow: /microsoft_outlook/confirm + IAP fallback /microsoft_outlook/iap_confirm + CSRF + email-match verification
behavioral_notes.observation: open_microsoft_outlook_uri (admin-only, requires a valid normalized _email_field address) returns an act_url to Microsoft's authorize endpoint. After consent Microsoft redirects to the /microsoft_outlook/confirm controller (auth=user), which json-decodes state, re-derives and consteq-checks the hmac CSRF token (_get_outlook_csrf_token, scope 'microsoft_outlook_oauth'), then calls _fetch_outlook_refresh_token(code) and writes active + the three token fields onto the record. For ir.mail_server it additionally re-fetches a token to read the id_token's 'email' claim and refuses the link if it does not match the server's email (prevents authorizing send-as for a different account). When the admin has NOT configured client_id/secret, on Odoo Enterprise (release.version_info[-1]=='e') it falls back to IAP: a GET to outlook.api.odoo.com /api/mail_oauth/1/outlook returns a Microsoft login URL, and the token comes back via /microsoft_outlook/iap_confirm; refresh likewise routes through _fetch_outlook_access_token_iap (/api/mail_oauth/1/outlook_access_token) so the client_secret never leaves Odoo's IAP proxy. On Community without credentials it raises 'Please configure your Outlook credentials.' This redirect/CSRF/IAP orchestration lives in the controller and is not metadata-derivable.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration -> Microsoft identity platform + Office 365 mail (gap #7, static)
behavioral_notes.observation: Outbound HTTPS integration via python-requests (3 call sites, no vendored SDK). It talks to login.microsoftonline.com (OAuth2 authorize + token; overridable via the microsoft_outlook.endpoint config parameter) for the credential lifecycle, and authenticates to Office 365 mail endpoints smtp.outlook.com:587/STARTTLS (scope https://outlook.office.com/SMTP.Send) and imap.outlook.com:993/SSL (scope https://outlook.office.com/IMAP.AccessAsUser.All) via XOAUTH2 bearer tokens. The admin supplies microsoft_outlook_client_id (public) + microsoft_outlook_client_secret (ir.config_parameter); on Enterprise an Odoo-hosted IAP proxy at outlook.api.odoo.com brokers OAuth so a self-registered Azure app is optional. This external SaaS dependency (Microsoft Entra ID + Office 365) is the defining trait of the module and is invisible to Python model/field metadata.

classification.rationale: microsoft_outlook is mail-infrastructure integration plumbing: it adds no business object of its own. It contributes one AbstractModel mixin (microsoft.outlook.mixin) carrying OAuth token state, two Selection options ('outlook') and protocol-login overrides on the inherited ir.mail_server (SMTP) and fetchmail.server (IMAP), plus two ir.config_parameter credentials on res.config.settings -- and it produces no sellable output. Its whole reason to exist is to authenticate Odoo's existing mail transport to an external SaaS (Microsoft Entra ID + Office 365) via OAuth2 and XOAUTH2 in place of a password. Per Stabell & Fjeldstad this is a support / firm-infrastructure function (value_model=support, activity_class=support); it is the direct sibling of google_gmail (the Gmail XOAUTH2 equivalent it even imports get_iap_error_message from) and of microsoft_calendar (the same OAuth-connector shape). For APQC it maps to 8.0 Manage Information Technology, specifically the external-system integration / credential-lifecycle band: the module manages an OAuth2 authorization-code + refresh-token lifecycle (login.microsoftonline.com), brokers credentials (client_id/secret, optionally via the outlook.api.odoo.com IAP proxy), and adapts mail authentication to a third party (gap #7) -- IT-management concerns, not business-capability development. The auto-architect baseline inherited 13.0 Develop and Manage Business Capabilities from the mail parent; 13.0 is rejected here because nothing in this module develops a new business capability -- it operates an external authentication interface for an existing capability (sending/receiving email), which is exactly what 8.0 covers. 9.4 'Manage IT-related risk / manage IT security' (a sub-band of 8/9) was the closest alternative given the CSRF guard, group_system-scoped secrets and id_token email-match anti-spoof checks, but it was rejected as too narrow: those security controls are protective details of the integration, not the module's purpose, which is operating the integration itself -- 8.0 (manage IT integration / interoperability) is the better top-level fit. This mirrors microsoft_calendar's deliberate departure from its parent's 13.0 to 8.0.

standard_capabilities: OAuth2 connect of an Outlook / Microsoft 365 mailbox (offline_access -> refresh token; scopes SMTP.Send and IMAP.AccessAsUser.All)
Outgoing mail via Office 365 SMTP (smtp.outlook.com:587 STARTTLS) authenticated with XOAUTH2
Incoming mail via Office 365 IMAP (imap.outlook.com:993 SSL) authenticated with XOAUTH2
Automatic just-in-time access-token refresh from the stored refresh token at each send/fetch
Admin-configured Azure app (client id/secret in Settings) or zero-config OAuth via Odoo IAP on Enterprise
CSRF-protected OAuth callback and email-match verification to prevent send-as spoofing
typical_fits: tenant that disabled basic/password SMTP-IMAP auth and mandates Modern Authentication (OAuth2) for mail
single shared outgoing + incoming company mailbox linked by an administrator
individual users wiring a personal outgoing Outlook server (res.users outgoing_mail_server_type='outlook')
Odoo Enterprise customers using the built-in IAP broker instead of registering their own Azure app
common_gaps: Community edition without an Azure app cannot use IAP -- admin must register client id/secret (UserError otherwise)
only the mailbox owner's own address can send (from_filter pinned to smtp_user) unless a mail.default.from system parameter is set
Outlook flags bursts as spam -- outgoing rate is capped low (default 10/min); high-volume sending needs a dedicated relay
scopes fixed to SMTP.Send / IMAP.AccessAsUser.All -- no shared-mailbox / send-on-behalf delegation handling
Azure app consent / admin-consent and redirect-URI registration is an external Microsoft-side setup step not done from Odoo
no POP path for Outlook (incoming is forced to IMAP); token refresh failures surface only as UserError at send/fetch time

open_questions: Exact behavior when a refresh_token is revoked Microsoft-side (e.g. password change / admin consent withdrawal): the user-visible failure path beyond the UserError raised at next send/fetch.

Whether the IAP broker (outlook.api.odoo.com) rotates/persists the refresh_token symmetrically with the direct-credential path, and how _fetch_outlook_access_token_iap behaves when its response omits id_token (used by the email-match check).
How send-as for a shared mailbox or an alias is intended to be configured given from_filter is pinned to smtp_user and the id_token email-match guard rejects mismatched addresses.
